mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the Federal Funds rate above 5.25% in the month prior to the decision is associated with a near-term negative S&P 500 20-day forward return due to tightened financial conditions and reduced risk appetite.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS crosses above 5.25% in the month before decision
regime_hint: Rising Fed Funds rate in late-cycle tightening phase
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not statistically different from the pre-signal average (t-test p > 0.05) during the identified tightening phase.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in UNRATE exceeding 0.15 percentage points for two consecutive months predicts a positive S&P 500 60-day forward return as labor market cooling is interpreted as a sign of economic softening and lower growth risk.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE increases by >0.15pp for two consecutive months ending before decision
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are negative or flat despite the UNRATE signal, with a p-value > 0.05 in a rolling regression.

mechanism_narrative: When the monthly HOUST index falls by at least 3% from its prior month within the same quarter, it indicates accelerating inventory drawdowns and a positive S&P 20-day forward return as firms are forced to raise prices.
candidate_trigger: HOUST decreases by ≥3% month-over-month in the current quarter
failure_condition: No significant positive 20-day forward return in the 30-day window following the signal (bootstrap CI does not include zero).

mechanism_narrative: A monthly INDPRO reading above 105 (2017=100) suggests robust manufacturing activity, which, when combined with a rising GDPC1 demand proxy, produces a positive S&P 60-day forward return as market anticipates sustained growth.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are negative in >50% of windows where both INDPRO > 105 and GDPC1 is rising.

mechanism_narrative: Consecutive months of FEDFUNDS below 4% and CPIAUCSL above 303 (1982=100) indicate a disinflationary stance, which predicts a negative S&P 5-day forward return as market anticipates short-term rate cuts.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS < 4% for two consecutive months AND CPIAUCSL > 303 for the same months
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are not statistically negative (p > 0.05) during the identified window.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp drop in PAYEMS by at least 10,000 monthly coinciding with a one-month RSAFS decline of >200,000 signals labor market stress, which precedes a negative S&P 20-day forward return as investors reassess equities.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS decreases by ≥10,000 AND RSAFS decreases by >200,000 in the same month
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.05) in the 30-day window following the signal.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly CPIAUCSL reading above 310 (1982=100) with no prior month above 305 forms a bullish breakout, predicting a positive S&P 5-day forward return as inflation expectations rise and risk premia fall.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL crosses above 310 without a prior month above 305
failure_condition: 5-day forward return is not positive or statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When INDPRO remains flat for three consecutive months while HOUST declines by at least 5%, it signals supply-side weakness that precedes a negative S&P 20-day forward return as investors anticipate slower growth.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO is flat for 3 consecutive months AND HOUST decreases by ≥5% in the same period
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not statistically negative (p > 0.05) during the 60-day post-signal window.
